issue.title: Follow the organization default stack config mode in stack init and new
issue.body:
Part of CDP-2715. On master `pulumi stack init` and `pulumi new` create a classic stack unless you pass `--esc-config`. With this PR they send `configMode: "default"` and the service picks based on the org's default stack config mode. `--static-config` opts out.

Nothing changes for an org until its admin sets the default to ESC, which the service only allows for orgs with managed environments enabled. Every org starts on static. An old or self-hosted service ignores `configMode` and returns no managed env, so the CLI treats the stack as classic and writes the stack file exactly like today.

- `--yes`, CI and scripts follow the org default too. Automation API runs (`PULUMI_AUTOMATION_API`) send `"static"` until the Automation API supports managed stacks (inline programs lose the stack file with their temp workdir)
- `--esc-config` keeps sending `createManagedEnvironment` rather than `configMode: "esc"`, since services from before `configMode` understand it
- When the org defaults to ESC and the env can't be created (an env with the stack's name, no permission to create envs), the service returns an error that points at `--static-config`. The CLI doesn't retry as classic
- The CLI sends `"static"` on its own where a managed stack would be refused: JSON stack file, existing config or secrets provider settings, a non-default secrets provider, `--remote-config`, `--copy-config-from`. Only in those cases it reads the org's default from org metadata and, when it's ESC, says which of these kept the stack in its stack file. A failed lookup just skips the notice
- The placeholder write and the "Created environment" line key on what the service returned, not on the flag
- Other `CreateStack` callers (`stack select --create`, the offer-new prompts, `up <template>`) send no mode and stay classic
- `--static-config` is left out of the generated Automation API, same as `--esc-config`
- apitype gets `configMode` with `default`/`static`/`esc` (`esc` is the same as `createManagedEnvironment` and the CLI doesn't send it)

Both flags stay hidden behind `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL` here. A follow-up PR shows them in help.

issue.title: Show the managed environment diff as an engine event

labels.name: user-2672266a/repo-e73cee9a
labels.description: This issue doesn't require a CHANGELOG update

issue.body:
Fixes CDP-2719

#25532 added the definition diff with no caller. This PR prints it: when a stack-managed env has local changes, the CLI renders the diff and sends it as a stdout engine event right before the engine runs, replacing master's one-line stderr notice. The format, secret labels and example output are in #25532.

What's in here:
- `ManagedEnvironmentNotice` and `PublishedDefinition` on the stack's managed env config, filled from #25532's `Evaluation`
- building the notice at config load, falling back to master's one-line notice if the diff fails so a display bug can't fail an update
- `runEngineAction` sending it as a stdout event, so `preview`, `up`, `refresh`, `destroy`, `import` and `pulumi do` all show it
- the interactive tree drawing download progress under system messages. Master gives system messages priority and hides progress, expecting them mostly during cancellation. The diff stays on screen for the whole run, so without this downloads would show no progress. On a terminal too short for everything, progress rows can push older system messages, including the cancel notice, out of view until the final frame.

`up` shows it in both its preview and its update, as it does for resources, and `up --skip-preview` once. `pulumi config` and `config get` print nothing, same as master.

Why the existing stdout event and not a new event type:
- the terminal, `--event-log`, the console update page and Automation `EventStreams` already render it
- the CLI already sends one from the backend for its own cancellation notice
- `preview --json` folds it into the digest as one info diagnostic, so stdout stays one JSON document
- a new type means changes to apitype, the console and every Automation SDK

Compared to the stderr line on master:
- it only goes out once the engine is about to run, so it no longer shows when the service refuses the update at start (another update in progress, a changed base revision)
- `--output json` drops it locally like every other event in that mode
- it's saved with the update's events, and stack read doesn't grant env read, so only `values.pulumiConfig` prints values. Everything else, imports included, prints its path with `[plaintext]` or `[secret]`

Other paths:
- Neo tools: handled in #25535, which adds stdout events to the logs Neo's tools return; without it the event lands only in Neo's events file and an env-only change previews as `changes: none`, same as master
- `destroy` outside the project and `up <template>`: refused on master before the env is evaluated

Known limits:
- Each changed preview still creates a draft (CDP-2657)
- The terminal shows the same redacted diff as the saved events, so changes outside `values.pulumiConfig` show no values locally either. That seems safer for Preview, and we'll revisit it for GA
- The interactive tree cuts System Messages lines at the terminal width; `--diff` and non-interactive output show full lines (logged in CDP-2582)

issue.title: Add a definition diff for stack-managed ESC environments

labels.name: user-2672266a/repo-e73cee9a
labels.description: This issue doesn't require a CHANGELOG update

issue.body:
Part of CDP-2719 On master a stack-managed env with local changes only prints "using local changes to environment X (based on revision N)", with nothing about what changed. This adds `stackenv.DiffDefinitions`, which lists the values that differ between the published definition and the local one, and `WriteDefinitionDiff`, which prints them as `+`/`-`/`~` lines (paths with keys as written, values as compact JSON) under a header naming the base revision. Both sides are decoded and compared by key and list index, so key order, formatting and comments don't show (a style-only change prints the header with "(no value changes)"). Nothing calls the diff or the new `Evaluation.PublishedDefinition` (the published bytes `Evaluate` already fetches) yet. Secrets compare by ciphertext and only get redacted when rendering, so a re-set secret (which publishes a new revision) shows up as `~ path: [secret] -> [secret]`. If either side of a change contains a secret, neither value is printed: each side shows `[secret]` or `[plaintext]`, so `[plaintext] -> [secret]` doesn't echo the old value into CI logs and a downgrade shows as `[secret] -> [plaintext]` without printing the new one. A rendered value longer than 256 bytes is cut and followed by its length, so a large config value doesn't put a megabyte line in CI or the update log. Non-graphic runes and colorize directives in keys and values are escaped so a definition can't forge or reorder output lines. Why diff the definition and not the evaluated config: - it's exactly what `up` publishes - evaluating the published revision is a second open, which re-runs providers and OIDC logins - evaluated values would show edits inside imported envs, which this update doesn't publish A 403 from the draft create now says `you need write access to environment proj/env to evaluate local changes to it` instead of `creating a draft of managed environment proj/env: [403] ...`. That covers every command that evaluates a managed env with local changes (preview, up, refresh, destroy, import, `pulumi do`, Neo tools, `config get`, `config --show-secrets`/`--open`). Other paths: - Printing the diff on preview/up, `--json`, Automation event streams and the console update page: a follow-up PR that sends it as an engine event - A user who can read but not open the env, with no local changes, still gets the service's raw 403 from the open (CDP-958)
Example preview and up output (with the engine event follow-up) ``` $ pulumi preview Previewing update (acme/dev) View Live: https://app.pulumi.com/acme/app/dev/previews/... Environment app/dev has local changes based on revision 3. up, refresh and destroy publish them; preview doesn't. + values.pulumiConfig["app:allowedCidrs"]: "10.0.0.0/24,10.0.1.0/24,10.0.2.0/24,10.0.3.0/24,10.0.4.0/24,10.0.5.0/24,10.0.6.0/24,10.0.7.0/24,10.0.8.0/24,10.0.9.0/24,10.0.10.0/24,10.0.11.0/24,10.0.12.0/24,10.0.13.0/24,10.0.14.0/24,10.0.15.0/24,10.0.16.0/24,10.0.17.0/24,10.0.18.0/24,10.0.19.0/24,10.0.... (2691 bytes) + values.pulumiConfig["app:new"]: "v" ~ values.pulumiConfig["app:pw"]: [secret] -> [secret] ~ values.pulumiConfig["app:token"]: [secret] -> [plaintext] Resources: 1 unchanged ``` `up` prints the same block in both its preview and its update, as it does for resources: ``` $ pulumi up --yes Previewing update (acme/dev) View Live: https://app.pulumi.com/acme/app/dev/previews/... Environment app/dev has local changes based on revision 3. up, refresh and destroy publish them; preview doesn't. + values.pulumiConfig["app:new"]: "v" ~ values.pulumiConfig["app:pw"]: [secret] -> [secret] Resources: 1 unchanged Updating (acme/dev) View Live: https://app.pulumi.com/acme/app/dev/updates/4 Environment app/dev has local changes based on revision 3. up, refresh and destroy publish them; preview doesn't. + values.pulumiConfig["app:new"]: "v" ~ values.pulumiConfig["app:pw"]: [secret] -> [secret] Resources: 1 unchanged Duration: 1s ```

issue.title: Encrypt config secrets with the managed ESC environment's key

labels.name: user-2672266a/repo-e73cee9a
labels.description: This issue doesn't require a CHANGELOG update

issue.body:
On a stack with an ESC-managed environment, `pulumi config set --secret` now encrypts through the environment's `encrypt-secrets` route and writes `fn::secret: {ciphertext: ...}` into the inline definition, and `pulumi config set-all` writes every value, plain or secret, into the definition the same way. This replaces the `set --secret` rejection from #25413, which routes `config set` and `rm` to the definition.

Every new branch first checks that the stack has a managed environment, so only stacks created with the `cdp-2941-iac-esc-managed-environments` flag on are affected. The `--json` reorder below changes nothing for other stacks, since `--json` can't be combined with `--plaintext`, `--secret` or `--path`.

- `ManagedEnvironmentsBackend` gains `EncryptEnvironmentSecrets`, a pass-through to the ESC client.
- `managedEnvEncrypter` adapts it to a `config.Encrypter`. The service returns the same base64 ciphertext `eval.EncryptSecrets` writes, under the env's own key, so it goes straight into the definition.
- The env comes from `ManagedEnvironmentRef()`, never the stack name, so a renamed stack encrypts with its own env's key. The tests use a stack whose name differs from its env's.
- `set`, `set-all`, `rm` and `rm-all` pick a config writer once per command: the stack file or the managed definition. #25413 checks for the managed store at each write and save; the first commit moves that into the writer with no behavior change. The managed writer has no stack secrets manager, so `GetEncrypter` is never called on a managed stack. That call can prompt for a passphrase, need KMS credentials, or change the stack file.
- `set-all` sends one request per secret, since its lazy `encrypt` closure takes one value at a time and batching would restructure the unmanaged path.
- A `--json` entry with `secret: true` and an object value is rejected before any encrypt request, since ESC has no secret-object literal. `--json` is now parsed first, so no sibling secret is sent before that error.
- `set-all` rejects `--config-file` on a managed stack, as the managed `set`, `rm` and `rm-all` already do, and runs the imported-key check from #25442 the same way `set` does.

One known gap for dogfood: `pulumi config --json --show-secrets` marks an object with a secret leaf as `secret: true`, so feeding it back to `set-all --json` hits that error. Each leaf can still be set with `config set --path --secret`.

Fixes CDP-2718

issue.title: Refuse to edit imported config keys on managed stacks

labels.name: user-2672266a/repo-e73cee9a
labels.description: This issue doesn't require a CHANGELOG update

issue.body:
On a stack with an ESC-managed environment, `pulumi config set`, `rm` and `rm-all` now refuse to edit a key that only an imported environment defines, and name that environment. A hidden `config set --override-import` writes the key into the stack's own environment instead, overriding the imported value for that stack, the same way stack config overrides an imported environment on classic stacks.

Part of CDP-2718

The check runs only when `ConfigLocation()` reports a managed environment, and only the service creates managed stacks, behind the `iac-esc-managed-environments` flag, so no changelog entry; this needs `impact/no-changelog-required`.

How the check works:
- It runs `CheckYAMLEnvironment` on a definition that holds only the stack's `imports`, so a broken local `values` block can't affect it. That evaluates without decrypting and runs no providers. A definition with no imports makes no call, and the result is cached per command, so `rm-all` makes one call for all its keys.
- The error names the import that defines the key (`Trace.Def.Environment`).
- A local key with the same spelling as an imported one is already a local override, and can be edited and removed.
- If the local key is `foo` and an import defines `proj:foo`, or the other way round, `set` fails, since the merged config would pick one of them at random. `rm` is allowed, since it removes the collision.
- Only the top-level entry is checked, so `--path outer.inner` errors when only an import defines `outer`.

`--override-import`:
- Writes the key under the import's spelling, so it replaces the imported value instead of becoming a second spelling of the same key, and prints which import it overrides. Without the flag, the error mentions it.
- Refuses a `--path` that reaches into an imported list. ESC merges objects key by key, but a local list replaces the whole imported list, so writing one element would drop the rest.
- This is the only way to override an imported secret for one stack: the managed environment can't be edited outside `pulumi up`, and a secret can't be written into the stack file by hand.

If the check call fails or returns any diagnostic, `set` and `rm` warn on one line and edit the local definition. One broken import doesn't block every `config set`, and the next preview reports it. The downside is that while an import is broken, `set` of a key that import defines writes a local override without `--override-import`. The ESC client returns no environment with the diagnostics, although the service puts the evaluated environment in the 400 body; returning it is a later Cloud Platform change under `pkg/cmd/esc/`. The diagnostics themselves come back inside an `EnvironmentErrorResponse` error, because #25397 fixed the missing `code` only for the open methods, so the warning joins the summaries from both places.

At merge with the config secrets PR (managed `set --secret` and `set-all`):
- Both add `org` to `managedStore` and set it in `managedEnvForWrite`, and that PR changes `managedTestStack`, which this PR's tests call, to return two values. Whichever merges second drops its `org` copy and fixes the call.
- In `config set`, keep the `overrideImport` line and drop the `--secret` refusal that the secrets PR removes. Secrets then go through this check too, and managed `set-all` runs it as well.

issue.body:
Adds an end-to-end integration test for stack-managed ESC environments in `tests/config/managed_environment_test.go`.

Part of CDP-2583

All seven subtests passed on a review stack running the full service, with the CLI built from an integration branch that merges the rest of this work. Outside that setup it needs the PRs below it in the stack and #25414 merged, and a service with managed stack create, GetStack, managed drafts and publish on update deployed.

- `TestManagedEnvironment` skips unless `PULUMI_TEST_MANAGED_ENV_ORG` and `PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN` are set. `PULUMI_API` picks the service and defaults to https://api.pulumi.com. The org needs the LaunchDarkly flag on and the Approvals feature (the edited-draft steps read and PATCH the draft, and those routes keep the Approvals gate).
- Nothing is wired into CI yet, so the test is inert in every existing job (see the questions below).
- Scenarios: stack init with `--esc-config`, plain `pulumi config` listing an env secret as `[secret]`, changed-and-applied, unchanged, stale base (409 "changed since it was evaluated"), edited draft (409 "edited after evaluation"), and a draft edit between draft create and open not changing the values opened by revision.
- `NewFromTemplate` runs `pulumi new <local yaml template> --esc-config --yes` with one plain and one secret default. It checks the stack file has no `config:` and holds both values under `environment.values.pulumiConfig` (the secret as an `fn::secret` ciphertext, no plaintext anywhere in the file), then that `pulumi up` records the managed env and that `pulumi env open` on the published env returns both values. ESC can only decrypt the secret if `new` encrypted it with the env's key, not the stack's.
- The stale-base, edited-draft and open-by-revision steps go below the CLI because it has no way to send a stale base revision or a pinned draft revision, and `pulumi env edit --draft` submits the draft it creates, which the service refuses on a managed environment. Draft create, edit and the pinned open use the ESC client; starting the update is raw HTTP, so the test checks the request body the service gets on its own.
- The raw update calls use an `http.Client` with a one-minute timeout, so a stalled response fails the test and the deferred stack removal still runs. On master `pulumi new` encrypts template secrets with the stack's secrets manager and saves every value under `config:`. With this PR, for a stack with a managed environment:
- Template defaults, prompted values and `-c` values go into `environment.values.pulumiConfig` and `config:` stays empty. Both the prompt path (`pulumi new <template>`, `--yes`, CI) and the guided path write through the same config writer `pulumi config set` uses (`cmdConfig.NewConfigWriter`).
- Secrets are encrypted with the environment's key, one `EncryptEnvironmentSecrets` call per secret, never the stack's. The `--esc-config` help says `--secrets-provider` only covers secrets in the state.
- On the guided path the closing summary names the environment next to the stack name, since that path creates the stack quietly and the "Created environment" line doesn't print. The prompt path prints that line itself.
- The credentials check uses the values `new` just saved, since the stack file has no `config:` to reload.
- `pulumi up` publishes the definition, as for any managed stack, once #25414 is in.

Checks that run before any template file is copied:
- `--esc-config` on a backend without managed environments (diy) fails.
- `--stack org/project/stack` naming an existing stack with a managed environment fails, with or without `--esc-config`, since writing template defaults into an env others may have configured would publish them on the next `up`.
- `--esc-config` with `--stack org/project/stack` naming an existing stack fails, since the flag creates a new stack.

issue.title: Refuse to edit imported config keys on managed stacks

labels.name: user-2672266a/repo-e73cee9a
labels.description: This issue doesn't require a CHANGELOG update

issue.body:
On a stack with an ESC-managed environment, `pulumi config set`, `rm` and `rm-all` now refuse to edit a key that only an imported environment defines, and name that environment. A hidden `config set --override-import` writes the key into the stack's own environment instead, overriding the imported value for that stack, the same way stack config overrides an imported environment on classic stacks.

Part of CDP-2718

The check runs only when `ConfigLocation()` reports a managed environment, and only the service creates managed stacks, behind the `iac-esc-managed-environments` flag, so no changelog entry; this needs `impact/no-changelog-required`.

How the check works:
- It runs `CheckYAMLEnvironment` on a definition that holds only the stack's `imports`, so a broken local `values` block can't affect it. That evaluates without decrypting and runs no providers. A definition with no imports makes no call, and the result is cached per command, so `rm-all` makes one call for all its keys.
- The error names the import that defines the key (`Trace.Def.Environment`).
- A local key with the same spelling as an imported one is already a local override, and can be edited and removed.
- If the local key is `foo` and an import defines `proj:foo`, or the other way round, `set` fails, since the merged config would pick one of them at random. `rm` is allowed, since it removes the collision.
- Only the top-level entry is checked, so `--path outer.inner` errors when only an import defines `outer`.

`--override-import`:
- Writes the key under the import's spelling, so it replaces the imported value instead of becoming a second spelling of the same key, and prints which import it overrides. Without the flag, the error mentions it.
- Refuses a `--path` that reaches into an imported list. ESC merges objects key by key, but a local list replaces the whole imported list, so writing one element would drop the rest.
- This is the only way to override an imported secret for one stack: the managed environment can't be edited outside `pulumi up`, and a secret can't be written into the stack file by hand.

If the check call fails or returns any diagnostic, `set` and `rm` warn on one line and edit the local definition. One broken import doesn't block every `config set`, and the next preview reports it. The downside is that while an import is broken, `set` of a key that import defines writes a local override without `--override-import`. The ESC client returns no environment with the diagnostics, although the service puts the evaluated environment in the 400 body; returning it is a later Cloud Platform change under `pkg/cmd/esc/`. The diagnostics themselves come back inside an `EnvironmentErrorResponse` error, because #25397 fixed the missing `code` only for the open methods, so the warning joins the summaries from both places.

At merge with the config secrets PR (managed `set --secret` and `set-all`):
- Both add `org` to `managedStore` and set it in `managedEnvForWrite`, and that PR changes `managedTestStack`, which this PR's tests call, to return two values. Whichever merges second drops its `org` copy and fixes the call.
- In `config set`, keep the `overrideImport` line and drop the `--secret` refusal that the secrets PR removes. Secrets then go through this check too, and managed `set-all` runs it as well.

issue.title: Block commands that cannot edit a managed stack's environment yet
issue.body:
On a stack with an ESC-managed environment, the commands that can't work with it yet now fail with one shared message before anything is loaded or written: "... is not supported on stacks with an ESC-managed environment yet" (`cmdStack.ManagedEnvironmentNotSupportedError` from #25374).

Part of CDP-2718

The blocks run only when `ConfigLocation()` reports a managed environment, and only the service creates managed stacks, behind the `iac-esc-managed-environments` flag. The `stack init` reorder below also affects classic stacks, so it has a changelog entry.

Blocked:
- `config refresh` replaces `ps.Config` with the last deployment's config and sets `ps.Environment` to a list of import names, which drops the inline definition. The check runs right after `RequireStack`, so `--config-file` doesn't skip it.
- `config copy` (`cp`) when either stack is managed, with the error naming that stack. Copying into one would write `config:` keys, which the #25374 check then rejects on every later command. Copying out of one without a key goes through `CopyEntireConfigMap`, so the destination gets the source's inline definition, the same problem as `stack init --copy-config-from` below; with a key it fails with "not found", since the source has no `config:`. On master only the destination's `IsRemote` is checked.
- `config env init`, the classic-to-ESC migration command. It builds a second environment from `config:` and appends it to the definition's imports, and migration is out of scope for dogfood.
- `stack migrate` from a managed source. It copies `srcPS.Environment` to the target as is, so the target would get the source's inline definition with ciphertexts keyed to the source env, which an anonymous open of the target can't decrypt. The check runs before the target is looked up, so no target stack is created.
- `stack init --copy-config-from` a managed stack. `CopyEntireConfigMap` copies `ps.Environment` whenever `Imports()` is non-empty, and `Imports()` lists `yaml` for any inline `values`, so this has the same problem as `stack migrate`. The source is now resolved before `CreateStack`, so the block creates nothing. On a classic stack this means a missing source fails before the new stack is created; on master it leaves an empty stack behind.
- `stack change-secrets-provider`, with a hint to use a customer-managed key (CMK) instead. It runs before `LoadProjectStack`.

`config env add` and `config env rm` stay allowed:
- `Environment.Append` and `Remove` have an inline-YAML branch that edits only the `imports` sequence, so `values` is untouched and the next `up` publishes the definition with the import added or removed.
- On the `stack init --esc-config` placeholder (#25385), `env add` writes a block-style `imports` sequence (tested).
- With `--config-file` both are rejected by #25413, because `up` reads only the default stack file.
- Before its confirmation prompt, `editStackEnvironment` lists config through `listConfig`, which on master can load the stack secrets manager and save. #25412 makes it do neither on a managed stack, and the commands that create one, #25385 and the `pulumi new --esc-config` change, merge after it.

issue.title: Write block style when an empty flow collection gains content
issue.body:
On master, a CLI edit to a stack or project file that adds the first entry to an empty `{}` keeps the flow style, so `pulumiConfig: {}` becomes `pulumiConfig: {'app:foo': bar}` and stays on one line after that. With this PR the mapping switches to block style when it gains its first entry, the same rule `pulumi env set` uses (`YAMLSyntax.Set` in `sdk/go/common/esc/syntax/encoding`).

Part of CDP-2718

`yaml.v3` can only write an empty mapping as `{}`, and `editNodes` keeps the original node's style. `stack init --esc-config` (#25385) writes `pulumiConfig: {}` as the placeholder for a managed stack's config, so without this the first `config set` would write it on one line.

This isn't gated and applies to any stack or project file, so it has a changelog entry.

- An empty `[]` and a non-empty flow collection keep their style.
- A mapping inside a flow collection stays flow, so `values: {pulumiConfig: {}}` stays on one line. YAML can't nest a block collection in a flow one, which is why #25385 writes `values:` in block style.
- A line comment on a restyled `{}` is lost (master keeps it), and on a `{}` sequence item it moves to the next item, as with `pulumi env set`. The `stack init` placeholder has no comment.

issue.title: Write block style when an empty flow collection gains content
issue.body:
On master, a CLI edit to a stack or project file that adds the first entry to an empty `{}` keeps the flow style, so `pulumiConfig: {}` becomes `pulumiConfig: {'app:foo': bar}` and stays on one line after that. With this PR the mapping switches to block style when it gains its first entry, the same rule `pulumi env set` uses (`YAMLSyntax.Set` in `sdk/go/common/esc/syntax/encoding`).

Part of CDP-2718

`yaml.v3` can only write an empty mapping as `{}`, and `editNodes` keeps the original node's style. `stack init --esc-config` (#25385) writes `pulumiConfig: {}` as the placeholder for a managed stack's config, so without this the first `config set` would write it on one line.

This isn't gated and applies to any stack or project file, so it has a changelog entry.

- An empty `[]` and a non-empty flow collection keep their style.
- A mapping inside a flow collection stays flow, so `values: {pulumiConfig: {}}` stays on one line. YAML can't nest a block collection in a flow one, which is why #25385 writes `values:` in block style.
- A line comment on a restyled `{}` is lost (master keeps it), and on a `{}` sequence item it moves to the next item, as with `pulumi env set`. The `stack init` placeholder has no comment.

issue.body:
Adds an end-to-end integration test for stack-managed ESC environments in `tests/config/managed_environment_test.go`.

Part of CDP-2583

All seven subtests passed on a review stack running the full service, with the CLI built from an integration branch that merges the rest of this work. Outside that setup it needs the PRs below it in the stack and #25414 merged, and a service with managed stack create, GetStack, managed drafts and publish on update deployed.

- `TestManagedEnvironment` skips unless `PULUMI_TEST_MANAGED_ENV_ORG` and `PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN` are set. `PULUMI_API` picks the service and defaults to https://api.pulumi.com. The org needs the LaunchDarkly flag on and the Approvals feature (the edited-draft steps read and PATCH the draft, and those routes keep the Approvals gate).
- Nothing is wired into CI yet, so the test is inert in every existing job (see the questions below).
- Scenarios: stack init with `--esc-config`, plain `pulumi config` listing an env secret as `[secret]`, changed-and-applied, unchanged, stale base (409 "changed since it was evaluated"), edited draft (409 "edited after evaluation"), and a draft edit between draft create and open not changing the values opened by revision.
- `NewFromTemplate` runs `pulumi new <local yaml template> --esc-config --yes` with one plain and one secret default. It checks the stack file has no `config:` and holds both values under `environment.values.pulumiConfig` (the secret as an `fn::secret` ciphertext, no plaintext anywhere in the file), then that `pulumi up` records the managed env and that `pulumi env open` on the published env returns both values. ESC can only decrypt the secret if `new` encrypted it with the env's key, not the stack's.
- The stale-base, edited-draft and open-by-revision steps go below the CLI because it has no way to send a stale base revision or a pinned draft revision, and `pulumi env edit --draft` submits the draft it creates, which the service refuses on a managed environment. Draft create, edit and the pinned open use the ESC client; starting the update is raw HTTP, so the test checks the request body the service gets on its own.
- The raw update calls use an `http.Client` with a one-minute timeout, so a stalled response fails the test and the deferred stack removal still runs. Both stacks' removals are registered before the command that creates them (`stack init`, and `pulumi new`, which can fail after it created the stack and env), and a removal that doesn't go through fails the test. Deleting the stack also deletes its managed env (pulumi/pulumi-service#51540), so a run doesn't leave envs behind unless that best-effort delete fails.
- Recorded metadata keys are checked on the update history (`pulumi.esc.managedEnvironment`, `.baseRevision`, `.changeRequestID`, `.draftRevision`).
- Test-only, so no changelog entry.

Opening as a draft to settle a few things first:
- Where should this run in CI? Other service-backed tests here (`TestConfigCommandsUsingEnvironments`, `TestRemoteLifecycle`) run against production as `moolumi` with the shared test token, and this would follow the same pattern through `getTestOrg()`. That needs the managed environments flag and Approvals on for `moolumi` in production, and it adds managed stacks, envs and drafts to that org on every run.
- Load on `moolumi` should be negligible next to the rest of the suite: each run adds two stacks and two envs per platform, and deletes them. If we'd rather keep new service-backed tests off production until CI can target staging (#22700 tried that and was closed), this can stay skipped until then.

issue.title: Add pulumiConfig value encoding for ESC environment definitions

labels.name: user-2672266a/repo-e73cee9a
labels.description: This issue doesn't require a CHANGELOG update

issue.body:
Adds `pkg/cmd/esc/pulumiconfig`, which renders `pulumi config set` values as YAML for the `values.pulumiConfig` section of an ESC env definition. It's the value half of the editor that `pulumi config set`/`rm` use on stacks with a managed ESC env, and #25379 adds the editor that writes these nodes into a definition. It also has `ImportsDefinition`, which returns a definition holding only the env's imports. Nothing calls either yet so this is inert.

It lives in `pkg/cmd/esc` next to the other ESC CLI code instead of `sdk/` since its only callers are the `pulumi config` commands.

`ValueNode` types values the way `pulumi config set` does: top-level and single-segment `--path` values stay as given, and a nested `--path` leaf gets `Map.Set`'s coercion (`"42"` becomes `42`, `"true"` becomes `true`, `"042"` stays a string). That coercion is unexported, so this adds one SDK method, `config.Value.ToCoercedObject`, which returns a value the way `Map.Set` stores it below the top level of a path. An integer above MaxInt64 is written to the definition with its exact digits, where a normal stack's file holds `1.8446744073709552e+19`; the program gets that float in both cases.

The tradeoff is a new public method in `sdk/v3`. The way to get the same typing without SDK API is to `Map.Set` the leaf into a scratch `config.Map` and read it back, which gives the same typing but takes some explaining: the scratch key has to be nested for the coercion to apply, and it can't be the real key or `Map.Set`'s `secure` sibling check runs against an empty map. Happy to go back to that if we'd rather not grow the SDK.

Values stay literal:
- `$` is escaped as `$$` in string values and object keys since ESC interpolates `${...}`
- `fn::` object keys are rejected the way ESC rejects them: an `fn::` key in any object, and an `Fn::` key in any case when it's the object's only key. A single-key `fn::` mapping is a function call in ESC, so a `set-all --json` object with an `fn::toJSON` key would turn into a call and the program would get a string, and ESC rejects an unknown one such as `Fn::GetAtt`
- A `{secure: <string>}` map is rejected at any depth, the top level included, since config reads that shape as a secret, and the next config read panics on it

`TestToCoercedObject` checks each value against what `Map.Set` stores at `a.b`, `TestValueNodeTyping` pins the integer above MaxInt64, and the editor's `Set` table in #25379 covers the rest of the `--path` cases.

Part of CDP-2718

issue.title: Evaluate the managed ESC environment when loading stack config

labels.name: user-2672266a/repo-e73cee9a
labels.description: This issue doesn't require a CHANGELOG update

issue.body:
On a stack with a managed ESC env, loading stack config now evaluates the stack file's `environment:` definition through a new `backend.ManagedEnvironmentsBackend`. An unchanged definition opens the published revision and a changed one opens a draft. The result goes on `StackConfiguration.ManagedEnvironment` so the update request can carry it. `pulumi config`, `config get` and the `--config`/`--config-file` flags get managed handling too, so none of them reads or writes config the env doesn't see.

Part of CDP-2584

Only stacks created as managed (behind the `iac-esc-managed-environments` flag) reach any of this, so no changelog entry and this needs `impact/no-changelog-required`.

- The definition check from #25374 runs first, so a missing definition, values under `config:` or a JSON stack file fail before any ESC call. `--override-env` is rejected after that.
- The env name comes from the stack's config location, not its project/name. After `pulumi stack rename` the link stays on the program ID, so the new name could point at an unrelated env.
- When a draft is opened, `GetStackConfiguration` prints "environment X will be updated from revision N" to stderr.
- Plain `pulumi config` only runs the definition check and the existing anonymous `yaml/check` (no draft). `pulumi config --show-secrets`/`--open` and `config get` (opens by default) evaluate the same way an update does, so on a changed definition they create a draft and need write access to the env, same as a preview.
- On master `pulumi config` and `config get` load the stack secrets manager and save the stack file whenever an env is present, which can prompt for a passphrase or need KMS creds just to list config. On a managed stack they do neither.
- When the managed env fails to evaluate, `pulumi config` and `config get` fail with the diagnostics in the error, as `preview` does. With the master code path, `pulumi config` would list config without the env's values and `config get` would report the key as not found.
- Env secrets are shown with `recursiveNopDecrypter` since `config.NopDecrypter` returns early in `Map.Decrypt` and would leave `{"secure": ...}` wrappers on nested values.
- `up`, `preview`, `refresh`, `destroy` and `import` reject `--config`/`--config-file` before saving anything. Those flags write `config:` in the stack file, which the definition check then rejects on every later command. `pulumi up <template>` on an existing managed stack is rejected before any prompt for the same reason.
- Outside a project dir, `GetStackConfigurationOrLatest` falls back to the last update's config. A managed stack returns the missing-definition error instead.
- `EvaluateManagedEnvironment` returns its own `backend.ManagedEnvironmentEvaluation` (httpstate converts from `stackenv.Evaluation`) so `pkg/backend` doesn't import `pkg/cmd/esc/stackenv`.

Release order: a CLI with this PR but not #25414, which sends the evaluation on the update, would open a draft on every managed-stack operation and never publish it. The CLI change that creates managed stacks (#25385) merges only after both.

issue.title: Add hidden `pulumi new --esc-config` for stack-managed ESC environments

labels.name: user-2672266a/repo-e73cee9a
labels.description: This issue doesn't require a CHANGELOG update

issue.body:
Adds a hidden `pulumi new --esc-config` that creates the new stack with an ESC environment managed by the stack, and writes the template's config into that environment's definition in the stack file instead of under `config:`.

`--esc-config` is hidden from help unless `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL` is set, like `stack init --esc-config`. The service rejects managed creates with a 400 until the org has the `cdp-2941-iac-esc-managed-environments` LaunchDarkly flag.

On master `pulumi new` encrypts template secrets with the stack's secrets manager and saves every value under `config:`. With this PR, for a stack with a managed environment:
- Template defaults, prompted values and `-c` values go into `environment.values.pulumiConfig` and `config:` stays empty. Both the prompt path (`pulumi new <template>`, `--yes`, CI) and the guided path write through the same config writer `pulumi config set` uses (`cmdConfig.NewConfigWriter`).
- Secrets are encrypted with the environment's key, one `EncryptEnvironmentSecrets` call per secret, never the stack's. The `--esc-config` help says `--secrets-provider` only covers secrets in the state.
- On the guided path the closing summary names the environment next to the stack name, since that path creates the stack quietly and the "Created environment" line doesn't print. The prompt path prints that line itself.
- The credentials check uses the values `new` just saved, since the stack file has no `config:` to reload.
- `pulumi up` publishes the definition, as for any managed stack, once #25414 is in.

Checks that run before any template file is copied:
- `--esc-config` on a backend without managed environments (diy) fails.
- `--stack org/project/stack` naming an existing stack with a managed environment fails, with or without `--esc-config`, since writing template defaults into an env others may have configured would publish them on the next `up`.
- `--esc-config` with `--stack org/project/stack` naming an existing stack fails, since the flag creates a new stack.
- `--esc-config` is exclusive with `--remote-stack-config` and `--generate-only`.

Failures after create:
- Any later failure before the config is saved (plugin load, the runtime-options prompt, the language template, encrypting or saving config) returns a message saying the stack and environment exist and to `pulumi config set` the values or `pulumi stack rm` the stack.

issue.title: Encrypt config secrets with the managed ESC environment's key

labels.name: user-2672266a/repo-e73cee9a
labels.description: This issue doesn't require a CHANGELOG update

issue.body:
On a stack with an ESC-managed environment, `pulumi config set --secret` now encrypts through the environment's `encrypt-secrets` route and writes `fn::secret: {ciphertext: ...}` into the inline definition, and `pulumi config set-all` writes every value, plain or secret, into the definition the same way. This replaces the `set --secret` rejection from #25413, which routes `config set` and `rm` to the definition.

Every new branch first checks that the stack has a managed environment, so only stacks created with the `cdp-2941-iac-esc-managed-environments` flag on are affected. The `--json` reorder below changes nothing for other stacks, since `--json` can't be combined with `--plaintext`, `--secret` or `--path`.

- `ManagedEnvironmentsBackend` gains `EncryptEnvironmentSecrets`, a pass-through to the ESC client.
- `managedEnvEncrypter` adapts it to a `config.Encrypter`. The service returns the same base64 ciphertext `eval.EncryptSecrets` writes, under the env's own key, so it goes straight into the definition.
- The env comes from `ManagedEnvironmentRef()`, never the stack name, so a renamed stack encrypts with its own env's key. The tests use a stack whose name differs from its env's.
- `set`, `set-all`, `rm` and `rm-all` pick a config writer once per command: the stack file or the managed definition. #25413 checks for the managed store at each write and save; the first commit moves that into the writer with no behavior change. The managed writer has no stack secrets manager, so `GetEncrypter` is never called on a managed stack. That call can prompt for a passphrase, need KMS credentials, or change the stack file.
- `set-all` sends one request per secret, since its lazy `encrypt` closure takes one value at a time and batching would restructure the unmanaged path.
- A `--json` entry with `secret: true` and an object value is rejected before any encrypt request, since ESC has no secret-object literal. `--json` is now parsed first, so no sibling secret is sent before that error.
- `set-all` rejects `--config-file` on a managed stack, as the managed `set`, `rm` and `rm-all` already do, and runs the imported-key check from #25442 the same way `set` does.

One known gap for dogfood: `pulumi config --json --show-secrets` marks an object with a secret leaf as `secret: true`, so feeding it back to `set-all --json` hits that error. Each leaf can still be set with `config set --path --secret`.

Fixes CDP-2718

issue.title: Refuse to edit imported config keys on managed stacks

labels.name: user-2672266a/repo-e73cee9a
labels.description: This issue doesn't require a CHANGELOG update

issue.body:
On a stack with an ESC-managed environment, `pulumi config set`, `rm` and `rm-all` now refuse to edit a key that only an imported environment defines, and name that environment. A hidden `config set --override-import` writes the key into the stack's own environment instead, overriding the imported value for that stack, the same way stack config overrides an imported environment on classic stacks.

Part of CDP-2718

The check runs only when `ConfigLocation()` reports a managed environment, and only the service creates managed stacks, behind the `iac-esc-managed-environments` flag, so no changelog entry; this needs `impact/no-changelog-required`.

How the check works:
- It runs `CheckYAMLEnvironment` on a definition that holds only the stack's `imports`, so a broken local `values` block can't affect it. That evaluates without decrypting and runs no providers. A definition with no imports makes no call, and the result is cached per command, so `rm-all` makes one call for all its keys.
- The error names the import that defines the key (`Trace.Def.Environment`).
- A local key with the same spelling as an imported one is already a local override, and can be edited and removed.
- If the local key is `foo` and an import defines `proj:foo`, or the other way round, `set` fails, since the merged config would pick one of them at random. `rm` is allowed, since it removes the collision.
- Only the top-level entry is checked, so `--path outer.inner` errors when only an import defines `outer`.

`--override-import`:
- Writes the key under the import's spelling, so it replaces the imported value instead of becoming a second spelling of the same key, and prints which import it overrides. Without the flag, the error mentions it.
- Refuses a `--path` that reaches into an imported list. ESC merges objects key by key, but a local list replaces the whole imported list, so writing one element would drop the rest.
- This is the only way to override an imported secret for one stack: the managed environment can't be edited outside `pulumi up`, and a secret can't be written into the stack file by hand.

If the check call fails or returns any diagnostic, `set` and `rm` warn on one line and edit the local definition. One broken import doesn't block every `config set`, and the next preview reports it. The downside is that while an import is broken, `set` of a key that import defines writes a local override without `--override-import`. The ESC client returns no environment with the diagnostics, although the service puts the evaluated environment in the 400 body; returning it is a later Cloud Platform change under `pkg/cmd/esc/`. The diagnostics themselves come back inside an `EnvironmentErrorResponse` error, because #25397 fixed the missing `code` only for the open methods, so the warning joins the summaries from both places.

At merge with the config secrets PR (managed `set --secret` and `set-all`):
- Both add `org` to `managedStore` and set it in `managedEnvForWrite`, and that PR changes `managedTestStack`, which this PR's tests call, to return two values. Whichever merges second drops its `org` copy and fixes the call.
- In `config set`, keep the `overrideImport` line and drop the `--secret` refusal that the secrets PR removes. Secrets then go through this check too, and managed `set-all` runs it as well.

issue.title: Add a pulumiConfig editor for ESC environment definitions

labels.name: user-2672266a/repo-e73cee9a
labels.description: This issue doesn't require a CHANGELOG update

issue.body:
Adds `Set`, `Remove` and `Find` to `pkg/cmd/esc/pulumiconfig`, which edit the `values.pulumiConfig` section of an ESC env definition. `pulumi config set`/`rm` will use them on stacks with a managed ESC env to write config into the env definition in the stack file instead of `config:`. Nothing calls them yet so this is inert.

They're built on `encoding.YAMLSyntax`, the same editor `esc env set` uses, so comments and formatting on untouched nodes survive a save. `Set` takes a node from `ValueNode`, so values follow `pulumi config set`'s typing.

Edits follow the same rules as `pulumi config set` on a regular stack:
- Both entry spellings (`foo` and `proj:foo`) are matched. `Set` fails if both exist since the config read would pick one at random, and `Remove` removes both
- `$` is escaped as `$$` in entry names and path segments, and `fn::` names and segments are rejected in any case, since a new one can be the only key in its mapping, where ESC rejects `Fn::` too
- `Set` refuses a `--path` write inside a function call such as `fn::open` at any depth, and a new key when `values` or `pulumiConfig` is itself a function call, since ESC rejects a function key with siblings
- `Set` and `Remove` refuse to leave a mapping whose only key is `secure` with a string value, since the next config read panics on that shape, and `Remove` refuses to leave a mapping whose only key is an `Fn::` key, since ESC rejects that. `Remove` checks every match before deleting anything so it doesn't half apply

There are four places where `YAMLSyntax` behaves differently from `config set --path`, so the editor adjusts for them:
- A null placeholder (`values:` or `pulumiConfig:` with nothing after it, from a hand edit) is reset to a mapping instead of erroring
- A scalar entry can be replaced by a container under `--path`, as config allows at the first level. A `{fn::secret: ...}` entry counts as a scalar there, and a non-null scalar deeper is an error
- A new array indexed past 0 is padded with nulls, as config does
- Removing under a missing parent is a no-op instead of an index past the end

Why not decode `pulumiConfig` into a `config.Map`, edit that and re-encode:
- It would drop comments, key order and formatting in a file people edit by hand
- Hand-written `fn::` calls and `${...}` references would have to survive a round trip through types that only model literal config values

Part of CDP-2718
